In this movie version, the kid accuses the women of a different "vice", because the producers didn't think the movie-going public was ready for a film about lesbianism.

glosses: To remove a bend so as to make, or allow to become, straight.

examples.text: to unbend a bow
He leant tensely against the corridor wall and frowned like a man trying to unbend a corkscrew by telekinesis.

glosses: To release (a load) from a strain or from exertion; to set at ease for a time; to relax.

examples.text: You do unbend your noble strength.
to unbend the mind from study or care

glosses: To unfasten sails from the spars or stays to which are attached for use.

examples.text: Unbend the rope.

glosses: To cease to be bent; to become straight.
To relax in exertion, attention, severity, or the like

examples.text: He spent the afternoon shaping a swagger-stick from the branch of jarrah and talking with Miss La Rue, who had sufficiently unbent toward him to notice his existence.

glosses: to enjoy oneself; to become affable and free from formality
